```{python}
#| echo: false
import base64
import html as html_lib
import io
import json
import re
from collections import Counter

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.io as pio
from google.cloud import bigquery
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display
from PIL import ImageDraw, ImageFont
from wordcloud import STOPWORDS, WordCloud

PROJECT = "portfolio-hub-464520"
DATASET = "dbt_prod"

client = bigquery.Client(project=PROJECT)


def bq(sql, job_config=None):
    return client.query(sql, job_config=job_config).to_dataframe()


# Fixed-order categorical palette (colorblind-validated) — never cycled or
# reassigned when the underlying set of topics changes.
CATEGORICAL = ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100", "#e87ba4", "#008300"]
# Single-hue sequential ramp for magnitude-only (ranked) bars.
SEQUENTIAL_BLUE = ["#cde2fb", "#9ec5f4", "#6da7ec", "#3987e5", "#256abf", "#184f95", "#0d366b"]
# Dark, muted moss green for the daily volume trend line.
MOSS_GREEN = "#4a5d43"
MOSS_GREEN_FILL = "rgba(19, 104, 69, 0.64)"
# Extra hues for topics beyond the top 6 shown in the trend chart, so the
# Top 10 Topics bar chart doesn't need a flat "everything else" gray.
EXTRA_TOPIC_COLORS = ["#4a3aa7", "#e34948", "#6b4226", "#1f6f78"]

# One shared chart style for every figure, instead of each chart cell
# picking its own font/colors/background. Matches the page's own type and
# palette instead of Plotly's generic default look.
INK = "#3f4148"
MUTED_INK = "#8a8d94"
GRID = "#eceae4"
pio.templates["gv"] = go.layout.Template(
    layout=go.Layout(
        font=dict(family="Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif", size=13, color=INK),
        paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        colorway=CATEGORICAL,
        margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=10, b=50),
        xaxis=dict(gridcolor=GRID, linecolor=GRID, zerolinecolor=GRID, tickfont=dict(color=MUTED_INK), title_font=dict(color=MUTED_INK)),
        yaxis=dict(gridcolor=GRID, linecolor=GRID, zerolinecolor=GRID, tickfont=dict(color=MUTED_INK), title_font=dict(color=MUTED_INK)),
        legend=dict(bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", font=dict(color=INK)),
        hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor="white", bordercolor=GRID, font=dict(family="Inter, sans-serif", color=INK)),
    )
)
pio.templates.default = "gv"


def finalize(fig, *, left=60, bottom=50, legend_bottom=False, caption=None):
    """Give every chart fixed margins, turn off automargin, and (optionally)
    add a small muted caption line explaining what the chart shows.

    Quarto dashboard cards resize the plot container while the page settles
    (fonts, flex layout). Plotly's automargin recalculates on each resize and
    can append new axis tick groups instead of replacing the old ones, which
    shows up as ghosted/duplicated axis labels. Fixed margins avoid that.

    The caption is set as the figure's own title (rather than a separate
    Markdown output stacked above it) because a Plotly figure fills 100% of
    whatever space Quarto's flex layout gives its output div — it has no way
    to know a sibling caption element already claimed some of that space, so
    the two overlap instead of stacking. Putting the caption inside the
    figure's own layout keeps it as one output with one height budget.
    """
    fig.update_xaxes(automargin=False)
    fig.update_yaxes(automargin=False)
    top = 10
    if caption:
        fig.update_layout(
            title=dict(
                text=f'<span style="font-weight:400; font-size:12.5px; color:{MUTED_INK}">{caption}</span>',
                x=0, xanchor="left", y=0.98, yanchor="top",
            )
        )
        top = 36
    fig.update_layout(margin=dict(l=left, r=20, t=top, b=bottom))
    if legend_bottom:
        fig.update_layout(
            legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="top", y=-0.3, xanchor="left", x=0, entrywidth=150)
        )
    return fig


def caption_line(text):
    """A small muted caption for non-Plotly outputs (image, markdown), which
    stack normally without the fill/overlap issue `finalize()` works around.
    """
    display(Markdown(f'<span style="color:{MUTED_INK}; font-size:0.82rem;">{text}</span>'))


# Global Voices flattens region + country + topic + format + language into a
# single `categories` array per article (see gv_taxonomy seed / int_article_tags
# model). mart_tag_totals / mart_tag_daily carry a `category_type` column so we
# can slice each dimension separately instead of treating it as one bag of tags.

daily_df = bq(f"""
    select article_date, article_count
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_articles_daily`
    order by article_date
""")

topics_df = bq(f"""
    select tag, mention_count, last_mentioned
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_tag_totals`
    where category_type = 'topic'
    order by mention_count desc
""")

regions_df = bq(f"""
    select tag as region_name, mention_count
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_tag_totals`
    where category_type = 'region'
    order by mention_count desc
""")

countries_df = bq(f"""
    select tag as country, region, mention_count
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_tag_totals`
    where category_type = 'country'
    order by mention_count desc
    limit 15
""")

top_topics = topics_df.head(6)["tag"].tolist()
topic_color_map = dict(zip(top_topics, CATEGORICAL[: len(top_topics)]))

topic_trend_df = bq(
    f"""
    select article_date, category_name, article_count
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_tag_daily`
    where category_type = 'topic' and category_name in unnest(@top_topics)
    order by article_date
    """,
    job_config=bigquery.QueryJobConfig(
        query_parameters=[bigquery.ArrayQueryParameter("top_topics", "STRING", top_topics)]
    ),
)

author_df = bq(f"""
    select author, count(distinct guid) as article_count
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.stg_articles`
    where author is not null and trim(author) != ''
    group by author
    order by article_count desc
    limit 8
""")

latest_df = bq(f"""
    select
        pub_date,
        title,
        author,
        array_to_string(tags, ', ') as topics,
        link
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.stg_articles`
    order by pub_date desc
    limit 15
""")


def strip_html(raw):
    """Drop tags/entities from content_html, leaving plain running text."""
    return html_lib.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", raw or ""))


# Site-wide boilerplate that would otherwise dominate the cloud: every
# article repeats an "Originally published on Global Voices" byline and
# photo-credit line verbatim, regardless of the story's actual content.
GV_STOPWORDS = STOPWORDS.union(
    {
        "global", "voices", "globalvoices", "originally", "published",
        "photo", "photos", "courtesy", "permission", "image", "images", "used",
        "read", "story", "said", "also", "one", "two", "will", "new",
        "including", "according", "told", "still", "even", "much", "made",
        "way", "years", "year", "first", "since", "like", "people", "may",
        "many", "us", "day", "days", "now", "say", "across", "without",
        "part", "hour", "hours", "month", "months", "three", "use", "used",
        "official", "public", "national", "local", "international", "around",
        "final", "become", "remain", "percent", "left", "right",
        "january", "february", "march", "april", "june", "july", "august",
        "september", "october", "november", "december",
    }
)

text_df = bq(f"""
    select guid, title, description, content_html
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.stg_articles`
""")

# Keep text per-article (guid -> lowercased text) rather than one big blob,
# so we can later ask "which articles mention word X" for the word cloud
# tooltips (see top_regions_for_word below).
article_texts = {
    row["guid"]: " ".join(
        filter(None, [row["title"], row["description"], strip_html(row["content_html"])])
    ).lower()
    for _, row in text_df.iterrows()
}
full_text = " ".join(article_texts.values())

region_tags_df = bq(f"""
    select guid, tag as region_name
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.int_article_tags`
    where category_type = 'region'
""")
guid_to_regions = region_tags_df.groupby("guid")["region_name"].apply(list).to_dict()


def top_regions_for_word(word, n=2):
    """Which regions come up most often in articles that mention `word`."""
    pattern = re.compile(rf"\b{re.escape(word)}\b", re.IGNORECASE)
    counter = Counter()
    for guid, text in article_texts.items():
        if pattern.search(text):
            for region_name in guid_to_regions.get(guid, []):
                counter[region_name] += 1
    return [name for name, _ in counter.most_common(n)]


word_cloud = WordCloud(
    width=1500,
    height=450,
    background_color=None,
    mode="RGBA",
    stopwords=GV_STOPWORDS,
    collocations=False,
    min_word_length=3,
    max_words=80,
    prefer_horizontal=0.9,
    random_state=42,
)
word_freqs = word_cloud.process_text(full_text)
word_cloud = word_cloud.generate_from_frequencies(word_freqs)

# Recolor with our single-hue sequential ramp (bigger word = more mentions =
# darker blue) instead of wordcloud's default random-hue palette.
_sizes = [size for _, size, _, _, _ in word_cloud.layout_]
_lo, _hi = min(_sizes), max(_sizes)


def _blue_by_size(word, font_size, position, orientation, random_state=None, **kwargs):
    t = 0.5 if _hi == _lo else (font_size - _lo) / (_hi - _lo)
    return SEQUENTIAL_BLUE[round(t * (len(SEQUENTIAL_BLUE) - 1))]


word_cloud = word_cloud.recolor(color_func=_blue_by_size, random_state=42)

top_words_df = pd.DataFrame(
    sorted(word_freqs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:15], columns=["word", "mentions"]
)

total_articles = int(daily_df["article_count"].sum())
days_covered = daily_df["article_date"].nunique()
topics_covered = topics_df.shape[0]
countries_covered = bq(f"""
    select count(*) as n
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_tag_totals`
    where category_type = 'country'
""")["n"].iloc[0]
top_topic = topics_df.iloc[0]["tag"]
```

## Row {height="280px"}
<!-- Article Volume over Time -->
```{python}
#| title: Daily Article Volume

fig = px.area(
    daily_df,
    x="article_date",
    y="article_count",
    labels={"article_date": "Date", "article_count": "Articles"},
    color_discrete_sequence=[MOSS_GREEN],
)
fig = fig.update_traces(
    mode="lines+markers",
    line_width=2,
    marker=dict(size=6, color=MOSS_GREEN),
    fillcolor=MOSS_GREEN_FILL,
    hovertemplate="%{y} articles<extra></extra>",
)
fig = fig.update_yaxes(dtick=1, rangemode="tozero")
fig = fig.update_xaxes(
    hoverformat="%b %d, %Y",
    showspikes=True,
    spikemode="across",
    spikesnap="cursor",
    spikethickness=1,
    spikedash="solid",
    spikecolor=MUTED_INK,
)
fig = fig.update_layout(hovermode="x unified")
finalize(fig, left=40, bottom=40, caption="How many articles Global Voices published each day. Responds to the date filter above. Hover anywhere along a date's vertical line to see the count.")
```

## Row
<!-- Word Cloud -->
```{python}
#| title: What Are Articles Actually About? (Word Cloud)

caption_line(
    "The most common words across every article's title, summary, and full text "
    "(site boilerplate and filler words removed). Hover the five largest words to "
    "see which regions they're most associated with."
)

img = word_cloud.to_image()
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

area_tags = []
for (word, _freq), font_size, (y, x), orientation, _color in word_cloud.layout_[:5]:
    font = ImageFont.truetype(word_cloud.font_path, font_size)
    tfont = ImageFont.TransposedFont(font, orientation=orientation)
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), word, font=tfont, anchor="lt")
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = x, y, x + bbox[2], y + bbox[3]
    regions = top_regions_for_word(word)
    region_text = ", ".join(regions) if regions else "no region data yet"
    tooltip = html_lib.escape(f"“{word}” is most associated with: {region_text}")
    area_tags.append(
        f'<area shape="rect" coords="{x0},{y0},{x1},{y1}" title="{tooltip}" alt="{html_lib.escape(word)}">'
    )

buf = io.BytesIO()
img.save(buf, format="PNG")
b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode()

HTML(
    f'<map name="wordcloud-map">{"".join(area_tags)}</map>'
    f'<img src="data:image/png;base64,{b64}" usemap="#wordcloud-map" '
    f'style="width:100%; max-width:{word_cloud.width}px; height:auto; display:block; margin:0 auto;" '
    f'alt="Word cloud of common words in article text">'
)
```

```{python}
#| title: Topic Trends Over Time (Top 6)

fig = px.area(
    topic_trend_df,
    x="article_date",
    y="article_count",
    color="category_name",
    color_discrete_map=topic_color_map,
    category_orders={"category_name": top_topics},
    labels={"article_date": "Date", "article_count": "Articles", "category_name": "Topic"},
)
fig = fig.update_layout(legend_title_text="")
finalize(fig, left=40, bottom=130, legend_bottom=True, caption="Daily article counts for the six most-covered topics, stacked. Responds to the date filter above.")
```

## Row {height="420px"}
<!-- Top 10 Topics Bar Chart -->
```{python}
#| title: Top 10 Topics (All Time)

top10 = topics_df.head(10).sort_values("mention_count")

top10_colors = {}
_extra = iter(EXTRA_TOPIC_COLORS)
for tag in topics_df.head(10)["tag"]:
    top10_colors[tag] = topic_color_map.get(tag) or next(_extra)

fig = px.bar(
    top10,
    x="mention_count",
    y="tag",
    orientation="h",
    color="tag",
    color_discrete_map=top10_colors,
    category_orders={"tag": topics_df.head(10)["tag"].tolist()},
    labels={"tag": "", "mention_count": "Mentions"},
)
fig = fig.update_layout(showlegend=False)
finalize(
    fig, left=150, bottom=40,
    caption="The most frequently tagged subjects across every article collected so far "
    "(colors match Topic Trends Over Time above for its top 6 topics).",
)
```

#| title: Regional Coverage

regions_sorted = regions_df.sort_values("mention_count")
fig = px.bar(
    regions_sorted,
    x="mention_count",
    y="region_name",
    orientation="h",
    color="mention_count",
    color_continuous_scale=SEQUENTIAL_BLUE,
    labels={"region_name": "", "mention_count": "Articles"},
)
fig = fig.update_layout(coloraxis_showscale=False)
finalize(fig, left=170, bottom=40, caption="Articles tagged with each of Global Voices' 11 macro-regions.")

<!-- Latest Headlines -->
```{python}
#| title: Latest Headlines

caption_line("The 10 most recently published articles, linked back to the original story.")

items = []
for _, row in latest_df.head(10).iterrows():
    date_str = row["pub_date"].strftime("%b %d, %Y")
    author = row["author"] or "—"
    items.append(
        f"**[{row['title']}]({row['link']})**  \n"
        f'<span style="color:{MUTED_INK}; font-size:0.82rem;">{date_str} &nbsp;·&nbsp; {author}</span>'
    )

Markdown("\n\n---\n\n".join(items))
```
